items: Case-study interpretation uses F_A=f(D_R*,B_F*,O_G+) and proposes ancestor-event signature Delta D_R*>0, Delta O_G+>0, Delta B_F*>0 under maintained/increased permeability.
Source explicitly says the cases do not prove ASEB; they test whether a common descriptive structure appears across domains.
Applications cover language, mathematics, scientific method, programming languages, evolutionary biology, AI, cross-case examples and non-ancestor examples.
ASEB interpretations attribute potential D_R*/O_G+/B_F*/P_E roles to language, mathematics, science, programming and biology and frame them as substrate/generator transitions.
Biological survival/fitness is distinguished from future evolutionary expansion.
Do AI systems increase future fertility via better learning methods, representations, reasoning operators and successors?

AI may gain capability while losing permeability; selected ancestor events are proposed to share fertility-component increases and to be substrate transitions improving future evolutionary conditions.
Cases lack controlled causal evidence, quantitative ASEB measurements, AI results, independent/counterexample sampling and validated ancestor-signature criteria.
F_A=f(D_R*,B_F*,O_G+) is restated as the central proposed fertility form under critique.
Source explicitly says ASEB remains uncertain/incomplete and depends on candidate variables becoming measurable predictors; criticism is part of framework improvement.
Limitations cover measuring F_A, meaningful distinctions, operator regress/direction, causality, substrate dependence, alignment ambiguity, stability tradeoffs and historical exceptionalism.

Open questions concern prospective fertility estimation, meaningful D_R*, genuine operator transitions, beneficial operator direction, discrete-vs-continuous depth, alignment tradeoffs and measurement/simulation/benchmarking/phase research.

Potential causal/counterexample tests include artificial evolution, controlled simulations, historical comparisons, searching fertility-reducing high-capability cases, and strongest falsification conditions.
Proposed depth spectrum: optimization Delta A, intelligence Delta Gamma, evolutionary intelligence Delta(Delta Gamma), ancestor intelligence Delta O_G+.
If strongest falsifiers hold, ASEB variables may be descriptive rather than causal.
Central revisable hypothesis remains that deepest evolutionary advantage is increasing future evolutionary capacity / escaping prior limits.
Prospective F_A, D_R*, O_G+, historical causality, substrate invariance, ladder discreteness, alignment, productive permeability, selection bias and executable falsification remain unresolved.
Definitions for adaptive continuity, D_R*, B_F*, O_G+, four causal-depth levels and final power/intelligence/evolution/ancestor hierarchy.

Evolutionary success is proposed as future adaptive capacity; capability can diverge from fertility; structural thresholds may create transitions; alignment is reframed through permeability/future value-generation; intelligence is linked to remaining transformable.
Future work asks for estimators, resource-vs-operator causal discrimination in major transitions, and structural conditions for evolution to create new forms of evolution.
Candidate metrics, proposed max-A vs max-F_A simulation, and removal-oriented ancestor evaluation are prospective methodological directions.
Ancestor-oriented systems may initially perform worse but eventually create larger capability trajectories.
AI evaluation is proposed to add future adaptive capacity—abstractions, learning procedures, successors and correction preservation—to current benchmark capability.
F_A and component metrics, ladder criteria, indicator validity, simulations, phase causality, alignment, removal tests and all prospective research directions remain unresolved/unexecuted.
